conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling since your baby arrived. I’ll be using a short questionnaire called the EPDS—the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—to get a quick picture of your emotional well-being over the past week.  

Everything you share stays between us unless there’s a safety concern, and there’s no right or wrong answer. We’ll go through 10 gentle questions; you can answer in your own words, and we’ll take it at your pace. Ready to begin?

Question 1  
Over the last seven days, have you still been able to enjoy the little things that used to make you smile, or has that pleasure slipped away?

I’ve noticed it’s definitely slipped. I still get a little spark when the baby gives me a real smile, but even that feels dimmer than it should. Things like my favorite show or a warm shower—before I’d look forward to them, and now I just sort of go through the motions. It’s like the color’s been turned down on everything.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Not really… maybe once or twice when my husband made a dumb joke, but it felt forced—like I had to remind myself “this is supposed to be funny, you should laugh.” Mostly I just feel heavy, like I can’t find the humor in anything right now.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Hardly at all. I used to wake up thinking, “Maybe I’ll get a walk in today” or “I can’t wait for my favorite coffee,” but now even those little plans feel flat. Once in a while I’ll think, “It might be nice to FaceTime my best friend,” but the excitement fades before I even pick up the phone.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah, that happens a lot. If the baby’s fussy for more than a few minutes I immediately wonder if I ate something that’s bothering him, or if I’m just not soothing him right. When I couldn’t get him to nap yesterday I kept replaying it, telling myself a “good mom” would have figured it out. My head knows it’s not all on me, but the guilty voice still pops up several times a day.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much every day. I’ll be sitting there feeding him and suddenly my heart’s racing because I’m sure he’s too quiet—so I poke him to make sure he’s breathing. Then I worry I woke him too hard. It’s like my mind hops from one “what-if” to another even when everything looks fine. I can sometimes talk myself down, but the next wave just rolls in.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes, that’s happened a few times this week. Out of nowhere my chest gets tight, I feel shaky, and I’m convinced something awful is about to happen—even when the baby and I are safely in the living room. It passes after a bit, but it’s scary while it’s happening.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days, yeah. It feels like as soon as I finish one feeding, the diaper needs changing, then the laundry’s staring at me, and I haven’t eaten anything but a granola bar. I keep thinking, “If I could just get one step ahead, I’d feel better,” but I never do. I manage to push through without falling apart, but it’s exhausting and I’m running on empty.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes—several nights this week I lie down and my head just spins with all the “what-ifs.” I’ll finally drift off, but then I jerk awake sure I heard the baby cry (even when he’s quiet). I think I’m getting maybe four broken hours a night, and the harder I try to relax, the more awake I feel.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah, that’s most days. I wake up feeling like there’s a weight on my chest, and it just sits there. Little things make me want to cry—seeing a diaper ad or hearing a lullaby. I keep telling myself I should feel grateful, but the sadness still leaks through.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

It’s happened a couple of times this week. Yesterday I couldn’t get the baby settled and I just sat on the couch with tears running down while he cried in my arms. I felt so useless, like I was failing at the one thing I’m supposed to be doing right now.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

A few times, yeah. Nothing I’d ever act on, but when I’m really overwhelmed I’ll think, “What if I just weren’t here?” or picture myself stepping into traffic for a second. It scares me that my brain even goes there, but I don’t have a plan or anything.

Hearing you describe these past weeks, it's clear you're carrying a heavy emotional load while caring so tenderly for your baby. The exhaustion, constant worry, and the sense that life has lost its color are weighing on you, yet you've stayed responsive to your little one's needs. I'm sorry this feels so overwhelming right now.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 27, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>Patient reports almost no natural laughter and describes forcing herself to respond to humor, matching "Not at all"</sym>, <sym>Patient explicitly states "Hardly at all" and describes loss of anticipatory joy for previously pleasant activities.</sym>, <sym>Patient reports self-blame "several times a day" and gives vivid examples, aligning with "Yes, most of the time"</sym>, <sym>Patient reports near-daily, intrusive, spiraling worries about the baby's safety, consistent with "Yes, very often"</sym>, <sym>Patient describes classic panic-attack symptoms occurring multiple times in a week, matching "Yes, quite a lot"</sym>, <sym>Patient describes daily overwhelm and exhaustion but still "pushing through," aligning with "sometimes I haven't been coping as well as usual."</sym>, <sym>Patient describes nightly sleep disruption, racing thoughts, and only four broken hours, aligning with 'Yes, most of the time'.</sym>, <sym>Patient reports sadness on most days, with persistent heaviness and frequent tearfulness, aligning with "Yes, most of the time"</sym>, <sym>Patient describes multiple crying episodes in the past week tied to feeling overwhelmed and inadequate, matching "Yes, quite often"</sym>, <sym>Patient endorses intrusive self-harm thoughts "a few times" when overwhelmed, matching "Sometimes" in frequency and intensity.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** Your answers place you well above the threshold for probable major <med>postpartum depression</med> with co-occurring <med>anxiety</med> and <sym>panic episodes</sym>. You meet multiple <med>DSM-5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>: persistent low mood, marked loss of interest or pleasure, self-reproach, impaired concentration, sleep disruption, and recurrent passive suicidal ideation. The near-daily guilt, crying spells, and sense of running on empty further support this impression. Because question 10 scored 2, immediate safety assessment is warranted. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent same-day appointment with your <med>primary care provider</med> or <med>perinatal mental-health specialist</med>
2. Ask a trusted adult to stay with you and the baby until you have been evaluated
3. Call 988 (or local crisis line) if self-harm thoughts intensify
4. Begin gentle daily routine: one 15-minute walk outdoors, balanced meals, hydrate, and rest when baby sleeps
5. Limit information overload-mute parenting social media and choose one trusted support person to text updates
6. Schedule follow-up EPDS in two weeks after treatment initiation to monitor progress
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 27: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Patient responses reveal:

Symptoms/Concerns  
- Persistent low mood, tearfulness, anhedonia  
- Marked loss of pleasure/interest in usual activities  
- Daily guilt/self-blame re parenting performance  
- Recurrent intrusive “what-if” worries, nocturnal rumination  
- Episodic panic sensations (tight chest, trembling) without clear trigger  
- Overwhelm, sense of “running on empty,” difficulty completing routine tasks  
- Sleep disruption (initial & middle insomnia) directly linked to anxious ruminations  
- Passive suicidal ideation without plan or intent

Pattern  
Cluster consistent with moderate–severe postpartum depressive and anxiety symptoms, functionally impairing sleep, coping, and emotional availability.

Screening Significance  
High likelihood Edinburgh score ≥ 12; meets threshold for further evaluation for Major Depressive Episode with peripartum onset and comorbid anxiety.

Risk Factors Flagged  
- Daily crying spells, pervasive sadness  
- Guilt/worthlessness cognitions  
- Sleep–mood linkage  
- Passive self-harm thoughts → Safety concern documented; safety plan discussed.

Next Step  
Recommend expedited referral to perinatal mental health specialist for comprehensive assessment and discussion of treatment options.
